# Operational Procedures - Bordeaux Control
> **Reminder**: This document is intended for use by air traffic controllers on the VATSIM network only and is exclusively for flight simulation purposes. It shall not be used for real-world air traffic control operations.
{.is-warning}

This section describes the internal coordination procedures between Bordeaux Control and the associated Approach units. It details the agreed coordination arrangements and the expected handling of traffic entering, leaving, or operating within the areas of responsibility concerned.

# General Coordination Procedures
## Transfer of Control & Communication
### Transfer of Control
Unless otherwise specified in this Local Operating Procedure, Transfer of Control shall take place at the common Area of Responsibility (AoR) boundary.

If the receiving ATS unit is marked as **BREAK** in EuroScope, the standard hand-off procedures defined in this Local Operating Procedure are suspended. In this case, transfer of communications shall only take place after the receiving ATS unit has assumed control of the aircraft using the appropriate EuroScope coordination function.

If an ATS unit needs to reduce or suspend transfers, the adjacent ATS unit(s) shall be notified whenever practicable. A minimum notification period of 5 minutes should be provided where operationally feasible.

While transfers are suspended, the standard hand-off procedures defined in this Local Operating Procedure shall not apply until normal operations have resumed.

### Silent Transfer of Control
Unless otherwise specified in this document, a minimum spacing of **5 NM** may be used for the silent transfer of control between adjacent sectors within Bordeaux FIR for aircraft at the same level and following identical or converging routes.

The transferring controller shall ensure that the applicable spacing is maintained for at least **20 NM** within the receiving sector and that separation is not infringed.

Whenever practicable, the same spacing should also be applied to aircraft inbound to the same destination at different levels in order to maintain a consistent traffic flow.

Subject to prior coordination, the required spacing may be achieved on average. In all cases, responsibility for maintaining separation remains with the transferring controller.

### Transfer of Communication
Transfer of communications shall take place no later than Transfer of Control.

### Hand-Off procedure
Unless otherwise agreed between stations online, the following hand-off procedure shall apply:
1.	The upstream sector sends the aircraft to the frequency of the downstream sector by voice or text.
2.	The upstream sector initiates a transfer via the appropriate function of the radar client.
3.	Upon initial call the downstream sector assumes the flight via the appropriate function of the radar client.

### SSR Code Assignment
Both ATS units shall transfer flights on verified discrete SSR codes. Any change of SSR code by the accepting ATS unit may only take place after the Transfer of Control point.

Where the aircraft is equipped and capable, Mode S identification using SSR Code 1000 should be used as the preferred method of identification transfer. Where the use of a discrete SSR code is required, SSR codes shall be assigned in accordance with the applicable ORCAM allocation or other VATSIM network-approved SSR code allocation scheme.

## Procedures for Coordination
### Definitions
A release authorizes the accepting ATS unit to climb, descend, and/or turn a specific aircraft by up to 45° before the transfer of control. Unless otherwise coordinated, the transferring ATS unit remains responsible for maintaining separation within its Area of Responsibility.

Unless otherwise specified, any reference to a VATSIM ATS callsign in this Local Operating Procedure also applies to any higher ATS unit assuming that position's responsibilities (e.g. APP procedures also apply when the corresponding CTR provides approach services).

References to ATS callsigns include all valid sectorized variations (e.g. procedures applicable to LFBB_US_CTR also apply to LFBB_CTR, and other sectorized variants).

| **ACC**     | Area Control Center               | **Kts**     | Knots                               |
| **AD**      | Aerodrome                         | **LoA**     | Letter of Agreement                 |
| **ADEP**    | Aerodrome of Departure            | **LoR**     | Line of responsibility              |
| **ADES**    | Aerodrome of Destination          | **NM**      | Nautical Mile                       |
| **AoR**     | Area of Responsibility            | **NVFR**    | Night Visual Flight Rules           |
| **APP**     | Approach Facility                 | **RFL**     | Requested Flight Level              |
| **ATS**     | Air Traffic Services              | **Rlsd**    | Released                            |
| **COP**     | Coordination Point                | **SSR**     | Secondary Surveillance Radar        |
| **CTR**     | Center/Enroute Facility           | **TMA**     | Terminal Maneuvering Area           |
| **FIR**     | Flight Information Region         | **UAC**     | Upper Area Control Center           |
| **FIS**     | Flight Information Service        | **VFR**     | Visual Flight Rules                 |

| **GND**     | Ground                            |             |                                     |

### General Conditions
Unless otherwise specified in this Local Operating Procedure, all aircraft shall be coordinated via the published Coordination Points (COPs) and transferred using a valid COP. Any deviation from the published procedures shall be coordinated between the concerned ATS units by voice, text, or EuroScope inter-sector coordination.

Aircraft shall be transferred at the flight levels specified in this Local Operating Procedure. If this is not possible due to the aircraft's Requested Flight Level (RFL), it shall be transferred at its RFL, provided no traffic conflict exists; otherwise, coordination is required.

Any traffic situation not covered by this Local Operating Procedure shall be individually coordinated between the concerned ATS units.
Unless explicitly released or otherwise specified, transfer of communications does not constitute transfer of control. The transferring ATS unit shall retain control until the transfer of control point is reached.

The following notation is used throughout this Local Operating Procedure:

- **↑FLxxx / ↓FLxxx** – Climb or descend to the specified flight level, unless additional restrictions are stated.
- **FLxxxA** – Climbing through and above the specified flight level.
- **FLxxxB** – Descending through and below the specified flight level.
- Any crossing altitude, speed restriction, or other condition shall be stated separately 	where applicable.

# Flights between LFBB ACC & LFBD APP
**LFBD APP** provides approach control services for **LFBD** and **LFBE**. It also provides flight information services for aerodromes with published IFR procedures, including **LFBS**, **LFBX**, and **LFCY**.

The systematic silent transfer of control described below may be applied without prior verbal coordination, provided that the following conditions are met:

For **departures**:
* Aircraft following **different trajectories** may be transferred silently provided a minimum spacing of **5 NM** is established and remains constant or increasing.
* Aircraft following the **same trajectory** may be transferred silently provided a minimum spacing of **10 NM** exists at the time of transfer and no overtaking will occur.

For **arrivals**:
* Aircraft may be transferred silently provided a minimum spacing of **10 NM** exists at the published Coordination Point (COP) and no overtaking will occur.

> **Note:** If a speed restriction has been assigned by the transferring ATS unit, the flight crew shall be instructed to report the assigned indicated airspeed to the receiving ATS unit on initial contact.
{.is-warning}

# Flights between LFBB ACC & LFBH APP
**LFBH APP** provides approach control services for **LFBH**. It also provides flight information services for aerodromes with published IFR procedures, including **LFDN**.

Unless otherwise specified in this document, prior coordination shall be carried out whenever the minimum spacing between aircraft at the transfer of control point is less than **20 NM** (or **3 minutes**).

Where reduced spacing is authorised by this document, the minimum spacing shall not be less than **8 NM**.
